title: Premarket · Friday 9/18

headline.title: Triple witching, and the board has exactly one thing to say: both classes of Alphabet are the only bullish kickers on it. GOOGL +2.24% and GOOG +2.19% premarket, 64 prints between them, zero bearish kickers anywhere — and the biggest early print on the tape is GOOGL $50M at the bid. Thursday answered the hike with a bounce: S&P +1.14% to 7,638, Nasdaq +1.69%, 10-year back under 5%.
headline.summary: Thursday was not a melt-up, it was a hardware rotation — and the order of it is being reported wrong. The newsletter has HPE leading the AI-server complex at ~8% “ahead of Super Micro's +6.1% and Dell's +3.4%.” Against settled closes that is backwards: SMCI +9.50% (36.85 → 40.35), then ARM +8.57%, then HPE +7.69%, then DELL +4.46%. SMCI led, not HPE, and ARM — unmentioned anywhere — outran both. None of the four had a company-specific catalyst. That is the memory bid widening into the assemblers, and the one hard number under it is MU on 9/30: MU tops cumulative dark-pool flow at $3.1B bid and the board's largest sweep is an MU $1000C dated 10/02 — expiry placed deliberately past the print.

overview:
Thursday delivered the relief leg. Claims 196k against ~208k expected, Philly Fed 37.8 against ~30. Yields retreated off the highest levels since 2007.

The sore spot was housing. August starts 1.275M versus ~1.41M expected — a clean miss, and the second negative housing read in two days after LEN. KBH reports next week.

Thursday's movers, settled: GNRC +18.34% on the Amazon deal — not the +21.4% being quoted. MRNA +8.55% on Phase 3 cancer-vaccine data with Merck. FLNC −15.36% on the guidance cut. CRWV −4.16% on a $3B convertible.

This morning's red is single-name, not tape. XENE −23.6% — paused new-patient enrollment in its depression studies on neuropsychiatric adverse events. NFLX −3.48% on a Wells Fargo cut to Underweight, $57 target. ACN −1.60%, Guggenheim to Neutral. STLD −2.10% and NUE −2.32% on soft Q3 steel guides.

Watch the index math today. SPY and DIA both go ex-dividend — $1.93 and $1.19. SPY shows −0.31% off Thursday's 762.64 print but only −0.06% against the adjusted close. That gap is the dividend, not selling.

Today: industrial production 8:15 · Bowman on stress testing 8:30. Earnings are empty. Triple witching does the talking — volume swells into the open and the close, and Wednesday's $266.7M CRM call block was pointed here.

XOM
Failed 2D stack · −0.7%

Six energy names are all Failed 2D — XOM, CVX, OXY, DVN, BP, plus GS. XOM opened 161.83, broke Wednesday's 162.56 low to 161.45, then closed 163.27, back above it.
161.45 is the line. Above it the failed break stands and the bounce has a floor; a close back under it says the sellers were right the first time.
A Failed 2D is a bullish reversal — new low, rejected, closed back inside. Six of six in one sector is not noise.
And it happened while WTI fell to ~$100.70, −1.7%, with Trump signaling the Iran war nears an end. Structure and commodity are pointing opposite ways.
That divergence is the whole note. Either crude stops falling and this stack is early, or the structure gives way — a $6.5M XOM options block says someone has picked.
NFLX
Lone red gapper · −3.48%
r
The only red name on the gapper board, down 3.48% to 72.69 with a $4.3M options trade behind it. Wells Fargo cut it to Underweight, $57 target.
No trade into an expiration Friday on a downgrade gap. The level to mark is Thursday's low 75.30 — it is already well below, so the gap is the range until it fills or fails.
The bank's argument is engagement trends and a weaker 2H 2026 content slate feeding lower margin expansion in 2027 and 2028. That is a 2027 thesis priced in one morning.
A $57 target against a 72.69 print is a 24% drawdown call. Targets that far below spot usually mark sentiment, not a path.
Watch it, do not trade it. Downgrade gaps on triple witching are the worst combination of thin conviction and forced flow.

Thursday was a 2U on 62.5M shares — roughly double the prior sessions' pace — closing at the top of a range that had been grinding lower all week.
No company-specific catalyst, same as HPE and DELL. It ran on the memory bid widening into the assemblers.
3.2x average options volume with a $2.5M block. The filter that called HPE Thursday is pointing here now — worth watching, not yet worth buying.
STX
$848M print · +0.29%
b
Thursday's largest single-name dark pool print: $848M at the mid, after hours. Biggest since NVDA's $1.2B on Tuesday.
Mid-side is interest, not direction. No level trade off a print alone — Thursday's high 816.68 and low 783.01 bracket it. Premarket 805.46, in the middle.
Storage and memory wearing the crown again, and STX sits in the Failed 2U group on Thursday's candle — it made 816.68 and closed 803.13, well under.
The stock is still 11% below its 9/08 close of 904.38. Size arriving into a downtrend is a different message than size arriving into a breakout.
Pair the print with price before reading anything into it. Right now price says the sellers are still in control.
AMGN
$131.4M put block · watch only
y
The largest options ticket on either board: AMGN $460P 10/16/26 at $131.4M. A floor put block, by a wide margin the biggest thing on the tape.
No trade. This is a note, not a setup — blocks this deep on a quiet mega-cap are institutional positioning or a hedge far more often than a directional call.
The honest read is that the size is the signal and the direction is not. A $131M put block can be an outright bearish bet or the other leg of something invisible.
It landed on a triple-witching eve, which is exactly when hedges get rolled rather than initiated. October expiry, a month out.
Worth knowing it exists so it is not a surprise if AMGN moves. Not worth $50 of risk on a guess about which side it is.

darkpool.note: The single-name tape woke back up on the bounce. Thursday's largest ex-ETF print was STX $848M at the mid, after hours — the biggest single name since NVDA's $1.2B on Tuesday, and storage-and-memory wearing the crown again with TSM $624M (ask) right behind it. The sides are two-way for the first time this week: Wednesday's top ten contained not a single ask-side print; Thursday brought the ask back in TSM and BE, with three at the bid and half the board mixed. Cumulative flow is the memory trade in miniature — MU $3.1B (bid) on top, into its own 9/30 earnings, then NVDA $3.0B (ask) and AVGO $2.1B (bid). Sit with that: the two biggest cumulative names landed on opposite sides. A side is a lean, not a verdict, so pair it with price. On the ETF board the trackers topped the tape again — SPY $1.1B (ask) was the largest print anywhere, the ninth straight session an S&P tracker has led, with VOO $973M and IVV $972M stacked behind it and all three at the ask. That is the flip worth naming: Wednesday's IVV and VOO printed at the bid into the decision, Thursday's printed at the ask into the bounce. Mid-caps came through IJH $428M and international through VXUS $342M.
darkpool.right_note: This morning's tape: GOOGL $50M at the bid, the biggest early print by a wide margin, landing the same morning both Alphabet classes own the only bullish-kicker view on the board. It gapped above Wednesday's high, took nine eighty six twenty, and closed above the prior high at nine seventy seven fifty. It tops cumulative dark pool at three point one billion on the bid, and the largest sweep on the board is a thousand strike call dated October second, two days past its September thirtieth earnings.
